title: Pin scheduler config for perf-canary traffic (disable experimental heuristic X)
author: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Context: The perf-regression canary runner is seeing higher-than-expected variance in tokens/sec and tail latency when the scheduler’s experimental heuristic X is enabled. That makes attribution noisy (regressions look like "scheduler drift" instead of "runtime build/kernel change").

This PR introduces scheduler config pinning for canary-tagged requests (source=perf-canary + request_class=canary_safe). For canary traffic we disable experimental heuristic X and lock a small set of scheduler knobs to reduce variance and improve regression attribution. Customer traffic is unaffected.

What changed: 1) Add a request-scoped scheduler override path keyed off canary tags: if request.tags.source == "perf-canary" OR request.labels["canary"] == "true", AND request_class == CANARY_SAFE, apply a pinned scheduler profile. 2) Pinned profile currently: scheduler.experimental_heuristic_x=false; scheduler.queue_shuffle=false; scheduler.batch_admission_mode=deterministic; scheduler.decode_fairness_boost=0.0. 3) Emit a new metric label for canary traffic only: scheduler_profile={default|canary_pinned} (gated behind canary tag to avoid global cardinality). 4) Add guardrails to ensure overrides cannot be set via user-controlled headers/params (only internal tags from the gateway / canary runner).

Why this approach: We want the canary to be stable and intentionally less "clever" so regressions correlate with runtime_build, kernel selection, GPU SKU, etc. We can still run separate experiments for heuristic X, but the baseline canary should be pinned.

Testing: - Unit tests for SchedulerConfigResolver: canary_safe + perf-canary => pinned; non-canary traffic => default. - Integration test in runtime-integration suite verifying that the pinned profile propagates through the scheduling layer and sets scheduler_profile label for metrics. - Manual sanity in staging: compared 30-min window before/after; tokens/sec variance reduced (stddev down ~35% on the 7B decode-heavy shape) with no change to median.

Rollout notes: Safe to ship behind existing canary tagging. The canary runner already uses canary_safe request class; if that changes, overrides won’t apply. This is intended.

Follow-ups: - Add a separate "heuristic_x_canary" workload if we want continuous monitoring of heuristic X itself. - If we need to adjust pinned knobs, keep changes limited to canary_pinned profile and include a note in canary runbook / dashboard annotations.

Refs: ENG-2854 (scheduler pinning), ENG-2846 (regression detector noise), perf-canary design discussions in #eng-runtime.
commits: runtime/scheduler: introduce SchedulerProfile enum and pinned profile definition
runtime/gateway-tags: treat perf-canary+canary_safe as eligible for scheduler pinning
runtime/metrics: add scheduler_profile label gated on canary tag
tests: add resolver unit tests + integration coverage
review_conversation: Noah Patel (review): Can we make the override depend on request_class=canary_safe as well? I want to avoid any chance that a future internal tool sets source=perf-canary and accidentally changes behavior for higher-volume traffic.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Good call. Updated resolver to require CANARY_SAFE. Added a unit test for source=perf-canary + normal class => default profile.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please add a note about maintenance windows / deploy annotations: if we tweak this profile later, it will look like a perf change. We should make sure it’s annotated somewhere.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Added changelog entry + internal doc note. Also added scheduler_profile label (canary-only) so dashboards can filter/annotate if needed.
Logan Wright (review): Label gating looks fine. One suggestion: keep label value set small and stable (default/canary_pinned only). Please avoid per-flag labels.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Agreed; only two values. No per-flag labels.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Any chance user requests can spoof these tags? We should ensure tags are only set by the gateway for canary and stripped otherwise.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Resolver only reads internal request_context tags emitted by the gateway auth layer; not from headers. Added comment + test ensuring headers don’t flip the profile.
Julian Moore (review): Can we also log the effective profile at debug level when canary tag is present? Helps when someone is looking at a single request trace.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Added a debug log line gated behind canary tag and sample rate (1%).
Noah Patel (final review): LGTM. This should help stabilize the baseline canary signals.
